In Shafer's '''dichromatic reflection model''',<ref name="Shafer1985">Shafer, S.A. [http://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/col.5080100409/full Using color to separate reflection components] Color: Research and Application, Volume 10, Issue 4, pp. 210-218, December, 1985.</ref> scene [[radiance]] has two components:

: <math> L(\lambda) = m_\mathrm{b} c_\mathrm{b}(\lambda) + m_\mathrm{s}c_\mathrm{s}(\lambda) </math>

: ''λ'' is the [[wavelength]],
: ''c''<sub>b</sub> is the body ([[Diffuse reflection|diffuse]]) reflected component,
: ''c''<sub>s</sub> is the surface (interface) ([[Specular reflection|specular]]) reflected component,
: ''m''<sub>b</sub> and ''m''<sub>s</sub> are [[scale factor]]s depending on [[illumination (lighting)|illumination]], view directions and surface orientation.

== Separation algorithm ==

=== BREN (body reflection essence-neuter) model based ===

Body essence is an entity invariant to interface reflection, and has two degrees of freedom. The Gaussian coefficient generalizes a conventional simple thresholding scheme, and it provides detailed use of body color similarity.<ref name="Je_ol15_bren">C. Je and H.-M. Park. [https://dx.doi.org/10.1364/OL.40.001940 BREN: Body Reflection Essence-Neuter Model for Separation of Reflection Components]. Optics Letters, Volume 40, Issue 9, pp. 1940-1943, May 1, 2015.</ref>
